step: cook the curd, crumble, ferment, salt
text: After the skim-milk curd is cooked and drained, it is crumbled and left to heat itself with yeasts before salt and caraway go in. No culture species is named in any source.

links.name: The Common Table: Pultost, a messenger from the past

steps.note: The curd is cooked, and it hardens into a raft as it nears 60 °C.
The crumbled curd is piled in a wooden trough and smells of yeast (acetone, banana) as it warms itself to about 34 °C in a 15 °C room.
Caraway is added with the salt.

processing.text: No culture species is named. The crumbled curd is piled in a wooden trough and warms itself to about 34 °C in a 15 °C room; farm versions ripen up to about a year.
